issues.legal_issue: In a land-revenue auction, the required initial portion of the bid must be deposited immediately in cash, and tendering it by cheque is not a valid deposit.
material_facts: The land was sold in proceedings to recover government dues as arrears of land revenue.
The highest bidder was directed to deposit one-fourth of the bid amount immediately and the balance within fifteen days.
The purchaser tendered the initial amount by cheque on the day of the auction; the cheque was encashed and accounted for several days later.
The balance of the bid amount was paid in cash within the stipulated period.
The landholder challenged the sale, and the Supreme Court considered whether the cheque satisfied the immediate-deposit requirement.
issues.conclusion: The cheque was not a valid tender of the required initial deposit. Because the mandatory requirement was not met, the sale was a nullity.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 285-D of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Rules, 1952 requires the purchaser to deposit twenty-five per cent of the bid immediately; on default, the property must be put up for resale forthwith. In context, “immediately” means without undue delay and within a reasonably prompt time, and “forthwith” requires resale without loss of time. The requirement is mandatory: Rules 285-D and 285-E are similar to Order 21, Rules 84–86 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, held mandatory in Mani Lal Mohan Lal v. Syed Ahmad. A cheque does not provide the certainty needed for immediate resale and may be dishonoured, frustrating the rule’s purpose. The Court followed the view in Hira Lal v. Mst. Champa and noted the similar view in M/s. Progressive Industrial Enterprises v. Bank of Baroda; the other cheque-payment cases relied on by the purchaser did not concern comparable provisions and were distinguishable.

predicates.land_revenue_auction: The property was sold in proceedings to recover land revenue or government dues as arrears of land revenue.
predicates.purchaser_tendered_initial_deposit_by_ch: The purchaser tendered the initial portion of the bid by cheque rather than depositing it in cash immediately.

issues.definition: When property is sold in a land-revenue auction and the purchaser tenders the required initial deposit by cheque, the sale is a nullity.
